cards.title: One sibling shouldn't carry everything
cards.body: Usually the one who lives closest ends up doing it all. Here are five ways to split the load so nobody quietly burns out.

cards.title: Split by task, not by guilt
cards.body: One handles doctor visits, one handles refills, one handles bills. Clear owners beat "whoever is free".

cards.title: Far away still counts
cards.body: The sibling in another city can book appointments, track refills and do the nightly call. Distance changes the job, not the duty.

cards.title: One shared record
cards.body: Keep the prescription, medicine list and reports in one place everyone can see. No more "latest parchi kiske paas hai?"

cards.title: A short weekly check-in
cards.body: Ten minutes on Sunday. What changed, what's due, who's doing what. Better than a WhatsApp fight at 11pm.

cards.title: Give the main carer real breaks
cards.body: Cover a weekend, pay for help, or have Papa stay with you for a week. Rest isn't selfish. It keeps the care going.

cards.title: Fair, not equal
cards.body: Everyone's share will look different. What matters is that it's agreed, visible, and nobody is carrying it in silence.

takeaway: Split caregiving by clear tasks, keep one shared record, check in weekly and give the main carer proper breaks.
share: Send this to the sibling group. Yes, that one.
